newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister urges peace on Corsica separatists.
newsitem.headline: French minister urges peace on Corsica separatists.

text.p: French Interior Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement, on his first visit to Corsica, urged separatist guerrillas on Thursday to stop their bombing campaign and he pledged economic growth for the Mediterranean island.
He said the message from France's six-week-old leftist government was "very clear" -- it could not help Corsica to emerge from its economic backwardness if bombings continued.

Both Corsican separatists and local criminals set off hundreds of bombs, which almost always cause no casualties, each year on the island to further their political aims or as part of extortion attempts.
Chevenement told reporters that the government's aim was "economic, social and cultural development" for Corsica.
But he added: "Nothing is possible without security, without an end to violence, without a definitive return to civil peace. Those who resort to violence must renounce it definitively."

Elected Corsican politicians denounced the previous centre-right government for conducting clandestine negotiations with separatist movements and Chevenement said: "The stand of this government is that there is no double-talk. There are no secret meetings."
Chevenement, who pledged an "open dialogue" with parliamentarians on the island, arrived in Corsica to a lukewarm welcome from separatist sympathisers.

Jean-Guy Talamoni, a member of A Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal front for the FLNC-Canal Historique which has claimed responsibility for many bombings, grudgingly acknowledged that "no door has been closed."
"We are ready to pursue the struggle with the means which have been at our disposal for years, but we are equally ready for dialogue," he said.
The FLNC-Canal Historique decreed a new truce on June 17, leading to an uneasy peace as the separatists await clarification of the new government's stand on Corsica.
